body: **2026-10-05-ci-gate-legs** — made ci.yml's `a11y` job ("Accessibility (a11y) tests") run `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh a11y`, which is `cargo test --workspace --locked` with a named `--test` list, in the slow tier, restoring the test job's cache and saving none (rows decision/a11y-ci-leg, decision/a11y-ci-gate). This is the leg invocation this chunk measures. It is a `--workspace` selection that differs from `-p blitz-tests` / `-p seven_guis`, and it shares the test job's cache. A mend that changes its cargo line is a CI-pipeline change pinned by `.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py`.

Watch for the same trap: a `[profile.*]` edit or a new `.cargo/config.toml` that shifts manifest lines cited by rows.

**2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — records the Dioxus feature wiring. The workspace takes dioxus-native-dom / dioxus-native with `default-features = false`, so a crate gets `accessibility` only by naming it. blitz-tests builds dioxus-native-dom with `accessibility`, and the seven_guis stand binary names none (rows decision/dioxus-accessibility-feature-by-name, decision/accessibility-feature-default-on). This is the root of the feature-unification differences between `-p blitz-tests`, `-p seven_guis` and `--workspace`, which the chunk's measurement must name.

**2026-10-07-driver-session** — escher-driver first entered the stand graph naming no dioxus-native-dom feature, and the entry that first read the snapshot through a session was to decide the feature. This is the precedent the act-by-id entry replaced (row decision/driver-requires-accessibility).

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — escher-driver names `accessibility` on dioxus-native-dom unconditionally, with no `[features]` table, so the feature reaches seven_guis and both its binaries through that edge. The reach was measured by dependency-graph reads before and after, and the lockfile was byte-identical (rows decision/driver-requires-accessibility, decision/stand-builds-no-platform-adapter). Bearing on this chunk: it shapes which feature set each package selection resolves, and so which metadata hashes it gets. No mend may drop this edge or add an adapter (`accesskit_xplat` / `accesskit_winit`) to the stand graph.

Measures from a cold build directory what grows it: which gate entries, CI legs (fast, a11y, stand-repeat, embolden, coverage, doc, build), the agent-run harness, the cold-agent pipe and the dev-host-only mutation tier write which artifacts, and which edits mint a new metadata hash for which units, read from cargo's own output.
Names the cause as numbers: the share of re-hash per low-crate edit, differing feature sets or package selections, profile or flag differences, per-file integration-test binaries and debuginfo weight.
Re-measures the overseer's figures (773 GB in deps, 193 test binaries of about 145 MB in 30-65 stale hashes) as hypotheses, not premises.
Applies one mend the measurement points at (one test binary per leg, a stale-hash sweep at a wrap or boundary, less debuginfo for test binaries, or another), with every check still green.
States a working day's growth after the mend in gigabytes, read before and after on the dev host (method manual).

body: The restructure's invariant: if the mend moves or merges the integration-test files into fewer binaries, every test keeps its assertions and its two layout modes, and the accessibility assertions (Rust tests over AccessKit), the stand contrast and focus-order tables and the stand expectation tables still run as before; the existing a11y, stand-repeat and fast legs hold it, all green.

The a11y CI leg and the accessibility test leg in the slow tier: its cargo invocation (cargo test --workspace today) is one of the invocations measured; if the mend changes its package selection, features or test targets, the leg still runs every accessibility assertion and still gates CI.
Accessibility checks gate CI: a mend that changes test binaries or leg invocations keeps the accessibility checks gating, and the CI legs' membership stays as stated.

Stand checks repeated three rounds: the stand-repeat leg (cargo test -p blitz-tests) is measured for its own hash; a mend that merges binaries or aligns its feature set keeps the three repeated rounds.

Feature unification across invocations: if the mend aligns feature sets between gate entries and legs to stop a second hash, the accessibility feature stays default-on, the session library still always enables accessibility, the browser accessibility feature stays off by default, the stand binaries still build no platform adapter, and the snapshot readers and screen-reader integration stay behind the accessibility feature.
The accessibility tier and reach stay as stated: a build-directory mend changes no accessibility capability and the reach statement is not edited.

The measurement: each step's growth read by size before and after from a cold build directory, each unit's hash read from cargo's fingerprint, message-format output or deps names, never inferred; the full workspace build's footprint read first; where coverage and the mutation tier write and whether they count toward the total read too.
The day's growth after the mend stated as a number of gigabytes for the capability v040-01, read before and after on the dev host, every check green.
Committed lockfile and --locked on every build, test and CI leg stay; a changed leg invocation is a CI-pipeline change that goes through the CI workflow pins and the test-target pins.
A stale-hash sweep, if chosen, touches the build directory alone: no new network, socket, environment read or secret; the mutation tier stays dev-host-only, never a CI leg.
Less debuginfo for test binaries, if chosen, still lets a failing accessibility or stand test report where it failed (line tables), and changes no test outcome.

body: Locked builds: the committed Cargo.lock stays, and every build, test and CI leg keeps --locked, including any leg whose cargo invocation the mend rewrites.

A changed workflow step keeps actions pinned to commit SHAs and read-only CI tokens; no new secret reaches any step.
Coverage stays measured by cargo-llvm-cov under the per-crate line coverage floors; where llvm-cov builds and what it writes is measured, not changed in meaning.
The blitz-tests crate stays unpublished, workspace-inherited in its dependency versions, with no git dependency added; its test harness takes no tracing and no style.
agent-run.sh selection still reaches cargo only as a test stem from its allowlist; a merged test binary leaves that allowlist check intact.
A stale-hash sweep, if chosen, removes only superseded artifacts inside target/ and nothing outside it: no following of links out of it, no removal of foreign files.
No new network access, socket, environment read or secret in any script, profile or harness the mend touches.
The mutation tier (cargo-mutants under nextest) stays dev-host-only and never becomes a CI leg.
The cold-agent pipe is measured only for what it writes to the build directory; its recordings, transcripts and checks stay owner-only and unprinted as they are.
Restructure invariant: integration-test files moved or merged into one binary per leg keep every assertion and both layout modes, held by the existing test suite and the blitz-tests targets check.
The measurement's output is sizes, hashes and counts of build artifacts only; it records no credentials and no page or screen content.

body: The build-directory growth measurement: each invocation's growth read by size before and after from a cold build directory, each unit's hash read from cargo's fingerprint, message-format output or deps names, never inferred.

Feature unification and package selection across invocations: workspace-wide test runs, per-package test runs, the embolden leg's added paint feature, and the no-default-features clippy run on upstream blitz-dom, each possibly resolving shared crates to a different hash.
Where the coverage tool (its own target subdirectory) and the mutation tool under the nextest mutants profile write their builds, and whether they count toward the growth.

The blitz-tests one-test-target-per-file layout and its manifest's test target list, which a one-binary-per-leg mend would replace; any merge of test files into one target must keep shared test modules out of the target list.
A test moved or merged keeps every assertion and its two layout modes; no change to what any test asserts, and the moved tests' existing checks hold them.
Test module paths and test names kept where files are merged into one target, so the CI tally of moves stays attributed by test name and a file joining a leg keeps its legs.
Every requirement still witnessed inside stand-repeat after any change of the stand tests' targets, and stand-repeat's three rounds and zero-failure budget kept.
The committed lockfile and --locked on every build, test and CI leg kept; the CI legs' membership kept as the invariants state.
A change to a leg's cargo invocation is a CI-pipeline change that goes through the CI workflow and blitz-tests target unit tests, which pin it.
CI legs keep running through the leg script, host-reproducible, under the fast/slow split and the shared build cache; the free-disk step on the test and stand-repeat jobs remains.
A stale-hash sweep, if chosen, touches the build directory alone and opens no network, socket, env read or secret.
The mutation tier stays dev-host-only under its nextest profile, never a CI leg.
Dev-profile debuginfo (line-tables-only today) and any reduction for test binaries must keep coverage floors per crate and the coverage leg's exit by the floors working.
The agent-run harness keeps its verbs, run selections, events and exit codes while any cargo invocation inside it changes.
The local pre-push gate and local baseline for CI comparison keep their meaning after the mend; per-package green is still not the workspace green.
The capability v040-01: the cause measured and named, a working day's growth after the mend stated in gigabytes, read before and after, every check green.
The test plan's harness and CI rows and architecture's test-crate layout restated where the mend changes the test crate's layout or a leg's invocation.
